I read the whole file (lines 1–108) and checked it against the rubric. I did not open any related source files and did not search the library for consumers.

The file defines the Prop-valued class `IsWellOrderContinuous`. It also defines two noncomputable `IsColimit` accessors, `isColimitOfIsWellOrderContinuous` and its primed variant. The rest is instances and one lemma, `isWellOrderContinuous_of_iso`, about transporting the class.

I found no function or construction whose homomorphism, continuity, equivalence or action structure is exposed only as separate facts. The accessors return a single `IsColimit` term. The instances for `f.monotone.functor ⋙ F`, `e.equivalence.functor ⋙ F` and the `Set.Ici` restriction are closure properties of a Prop class. They are not unbundled fields of a standard bundled structure, so there is nothing to bundle.

I did not flag `isWellOrderContinuous_of_iso`. Its conclusion is a Prop-valued class, and I could not support any bundled replacement or a consumer that would gain from one.

My remaining uncertainty is about uses elsewhere in Mathlib, which I did not check.
